claims.status_note: Replies welcome the news (#3, #4, #6, #18), but nobody confirms the agreement or dates with evidence or disputes them.
claims.text: NU7 has unanimous agreement among the orgs and engineering teams across the Zcash ecosystem, with testnet activation on October 6, 2026 and mainnet activation on November 5, 2026, including 25-second blocks, disabling v4 transactions and NSM integration.

claims.status_note: #31 independently states there are no changes to transaction formats or signing algorithms, and #32 accepts that reasoning for Keystone. #30 lists wallets that still need updates, but no post argues against this claim directly.
claims.text: NU7 adds no new transaction formats or signing changes, so it should not significantly affect wallets; mainly infrastructure such as full nodes, indexers and block explorers may be affected.

claims.status_note: #8 answers #7's question and quotes the ZIP-218 text; nobody else comments on it.
claims.text: Block rewards per block will be lowered to compensate for the faster block time, so total ZEC issuance per unit of time stays the same under ZIP-218.

claims.status_note: Nobody disputes or discusses the value of ZSAs; #11 and #28 answer #9's separate question about consensus.
claims.text: ZSAs would be a huge feature for Zcash and should be added soon as a new transaction format.

claims.status_note: Nobody replies to #11 directly. #28, answering the same question from #9, describes a consensus to prepare ZSA code but keep it out of NU7, without referring to #11.
claims.text: Consensus around ZSAs is still being debated.

claims.status_note: Nobody disputes it. #26 later gives arithmetic on how many 25 s blocks match ten 75 s blocks, but does not say whether exchanges should change their limits.
claims.text: Confirmation limits are set by each exchange; whether to extend them to compensate for faster blocks is up to them, and doing so does not seem very necessary.

claims.status_note: #16 accepts it ('That makes sense') and nobody disputes it, but no other source is given.
claims.text: After NU7 disables v4 transactions, Sprout funds will effectively be stuck and cannot be spent normally, and there is relatively zero chance of them being re-enabled through another upgrade.

claims.status_note: Nobody disputes it. #16 asks whether recovery could happen later and #17 repeats that any recovery would need some other method.
claims.text: What to do about Sprout funds after the pool is deprecated has been discussed repeatedly with nothing definitive decided, and a future Sprout redemption mechanism is being discussed in a linked thread.

claims.status_note: #21 answers the repository and timeline questions but does not address the sync finding.
claims.text: An unmodified WebZjs build cannot sync on the NU7 testnet because lightwalletd v0.5.4 returns a trailers-only response to an empty GetAddressUtxosStream, which tonic-web-wasm-client rejects as malformed; a workaround lets a ported wallet sync.

claims.status_note: Nobody confirms or disputes the figures; #26 presents them as numbers only, without assessment.
claims.text: Over NU7 testnet blocks 4,465,026 to 4,514,228, the mean block interval was 23.68 s against 25 s expected and the median 17.0 s against 17.3 s expected; 3.59 % of intervals exceeded 75 s against 4.98 % expected, and the longest gap was 451 s.

claims.status_note: Nobody responds to the figures.
claims.text: On the NU7 testnet, 5 of 6 hashrate jumps of 2x or more were followed by difficulty coming within 15 % of the new level after a median of 960 blocks; no timestamps went backwards and there was 1 minimum-difficulty block.

claims.status_note: Nobody responds; #26 notes the listener is one location and not a full node.
claims.text: In a 330-minute listener window, 5 of 780 announced testnet blocks did not end up in the chain, each at depth 1, and the first Zakura announcement came a median of 36 ms after the first Zebra announcement.

claims.status_note: Offered as measurement and arithmetic only, in answer to #13; nobody responds.
claims.text: Matching the expected time of ten blocks at 75 s takes 30 blocks at 25 s (32 at the measured mean); on testnet 30 consecutive blocks spanned a median of 730 s and p99 of 1,187 s, against 1,409 s p99 expected for ten 75 s blocks.

claims.status_note: Nobody responds. It does not refer to #11, which describes the ZSA consensus status as 'Debate'.
claims.text: ZSA code has been updated to Ironwood and 6.3 and is being delivered for testing; for the past year the consensus has been to get the code ready and have it on testnet but not include it in the NU7 deployment.

claims.status_note: Answers #27's question; nobody responds.
claims.text: The plainest change users will notice after NU7 is a shorter wait for the first confirmation, since testnet blocks average 23.68 s against 75 s on mainnet today.

claims.status_note: #32 re-checks the list and adds items (zingolib 8.0.0, Ledger Live 4.25.0, the NEAR Omni Bridge contracts, Zodl Android's SDK); nobody disputes it.
claims.text: Much of the ecosystem is ready for NU7: Zebra 7.0.0, the librustzcash NU7 crates, zingolib, BitGo, the ZNS mint and Ledger Live are ready upstream, and several other wallets have fixes waiting for review.

claims.status_note: #31 says it does not matter for NU7 because PCZTs carry the branch ID, and points to a migration PR. #32 concedes the concern 'doesn't hold' and updates the list.
claims.text: Keystone's firmware is built on a library version with no NU7 at all and no fix was in progress, which puts its ability to send after NU7 at risk.

claims.status_note: #31 says it does not matter for NU7 and that the update is in the pipeline. #32 concedes that Swift SDK 7.0.0 on the final NU7 crates went out the night before #30.
claims.text: Zodl on iOS is still on the NU7 pre-release crates, which do not have the mainnet height, and no fix was in progress.

claims.status_note: Nobody else rebuts it; #32 concedes in part: Unstoppable iOS is fixed (Android still pins the old SDK), Noir has an open NU7 PR (testnet-only), and the Trezor issue is a low-priority cleanup with no funds at risk.
claims.text: Unstoppable Wallet pins pre-NU7 SDK versions on Android and iOS, every Noir Wallet send has failed on testnet since activation, and the Trezor firmware issue is still open, all with no fix in progress.

claims.status_note: #32 says these still look the same after re-checking; nobody else responds.
claims.text: KeepKey firmware signs Ironwood spends only with the old NU6.3 branch ID, ShapeShift hard-codes the NU6.3 branch ID, Trust Wallet Core builds only v4 transactions and the original MIT Android and Swift SDKs stop at 4.0.0, so apps on them will not be able to send.

claims.status_note: Nobody responds.
claims.text: From 43,793 mainnet blocks up to height 3,533,510 (28 October), the mean block interval is 75.34 s against the 75 s target.

claims.status_note: Nobody responds. It is a statistical estimate from the c21 mean, not a stated schedule.
claims.text: At that pace the activation height 3,543,405 lands around 6 November 02:26 UTC, with a 90 % band from 5 November 23:01 to 6 November 05:51 UTC, so activation plans should allow for the whole band.

open_questions.text: What will the average circuit size (k-value) be under Tachyon? The question received no reply.
Can old Sprout funds be recovered after NU7, for example through a future redemption mechanism? Nothing definitive has been decided.
Will ZSAs be adopted in a later upgrade? #11 says the status is 'Debate'; #28 says the consensus has been to prepare the code but not include it in NU7.
Will exchanges need more confirmations at 25-second blocks? #14 says it is up to exchanges; #26 gives arithmetic without a recommendation.
Which wallets will be able to send after activation? KeepKey, ShapeShift, Trust Wallet Core and the original MIT SDKs still looked unready, and Unstoppable Android still pinned an old SDK.

overview.text: ebfull opens by announcing that NU7 is proceeding with unanimous agreement among orgs and engineering teams: testnet activation on October 6 and mainnet on November 5, 2026, with 25-second blocks, v4 transactions disabled and NSM integration, and no new transaction formats. The thread doubles as a checklist. Short congratulations follow, and one reader asks about the average circuit size under Tachyon.

Readers' questions are answered by moderators and support staff. Shawn says issuance per unit of time stays the same because per-block rewards drop (ZIP-218). On ZSAs, Autotunafish says the status is 'Debate', while _jon later says the consensus has been to ready the code and test it on testnet but not include it in NU7. On confirmations, Autotunafish says exchanges decide; on Sprout, he says funds will effectively be stuck after NU7 with nothing definitive decided, and vaspholdings points to a thread on a future redemption mechanism.

Tooling notes appear alongside: a Zakura dashboard, a zecd release candidate, and a WebZjs exchange in which etimpaul22 reports a testnet sync failure and Mari of red-dev names the correct repository and deployment timing.

PulseHawk offers independent counts of the NU7 testnet. After a first note on a 19.5 s dashboard median, it posts block-interval, difficulty, listener and confirmation-arithmetic figures as numbers only, then a CSV and a note on what users will notice. Zec85 asks what improvement users will notice.

Anirudh-712 posts a wallet-readiness list. str4d replies that the Keystone and Zodl iOS concerns do not matter for NU7. Anirudh-712 accepts both corrections, revises several other rows, and leaves KeepKey, ShapeShift, Trust Wallet Core and the original MIT SDKs unchanged.

Near the activation date PulseHawk estimates from the mainnet mean interval that block 3,543,405 lands around 6 November 02:26 UTC within a roughly seven-hour band, and Dpeluola shares a live NU7 page.

positions.label: NU7 is proceeding on the announced schedule
positions.summary: NU7 has unanimous agreement among the orgs and engineering teams, with testnet on October 6 and mainnet on November 5, 2026. Posters welcome it and look forward to activation.

positions.label: ZSAs would be a valuable addition
positions.summary: ZSAs would be a huge feature for Zcash; the hope is to see the new transaction format soon.

positions.label: ZSA status: debated, with code readied but kept out of NU7
positions.summary: Consensus around ZSAs is still being debated. Code has been updated to Ironwood and 6.3 for testing, and the past year's consensus was to have it on testnet but not in the NU7 deployment.

positions.label: Confirmation counts are for exchanges to decide
positions.summary: Each exchange sets its own confirmation limits; extending them to compensate for faster blocks is up to them and does not seem very necessary.

positions.label: Sprout funds become stuck after NU7; recovery is undecided
positions.summary: After NU7 disables v4 transactions Sprout funds cannot be spent normally, and re-enabling them through another upgrade is very unlikely. Any recovery would come from another method, and a future redemption mechanism is being discussed elsewhere.

positions.label: Independent counts of testnet and mainnet block timing
positions.summary: PulseHawk reports measured intervals, difficulty behavior, propagation and confirmation arithmetic for the NU7 testnet, presented as numbers only without assessment, and a mainnet-based estimate of when the activation height arrives.

positions.label: Some wallets may not be ready, so track readiness
positions.summary: A public-evidence list shows many wallets ready but several, including KeepKey, ShapeShift, Trust Wallet Core and the original MIT SDKs, without NU7 support; 'ready' means merged or released upstream, and users still need their wallet's update.

positions.label: Keystone and Zodl iOS concerns do not matter for NU7
positions.summary: NU7 changes no transaction formats or signing algorithms and PCZTs carry the target consensus branch ID, so existing Keystone firmware works after NU7; a migration PR is already up and the Zodl update is in the pipeline.

summary.tldr: Announcement thread for NU7: mainnet activation is set for Nov 5, 2026 with 25-second blocks and v4 transactions disabled. Replies are mostly questions (issuance, confirmations, Sprout funds, ZSAs), independent block-time counts and a wallet-readiness list that was partly corrected in-thread.
